chunks.arabic_text: ٢٦ - الْمَعْلَى بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ، الْبَصْرِيُّ، أَبُو مُحَمَّدٍ. يُعْرَفُ حَدِيثُهُ، وَيُنْكَرُ. وَيَرْوِي عَنِ الضُّعَفَاءِ وَيُجَازُ أَنْ يُخْرَجَ شَاهِدًا.

translations.en: 26 – Al-Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, al-Baṣrī, Abū Muḥammad. His ḥadīth are recognized and denied. He narrates from the weak narrators. It is permissible for him to be brought out as a witness.

en.summary: Al-Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad al-Baṣrī is characterized in al-Ghadāʾirī’s *Kitab al-Duʿafāʾ* as a narrator of intermediate status, whose reliability is contingent upon the strength of his sources. By primarily narrating from weak transmitters, his hadiths are deemed insufficient for establishing independent legal rulings (hujjah) but remain valid for use as corroborating evidence (shahādah) to strengthen other chains. This classification reflects the nuanced Shia methodology of evaluating narrators not merely as 'weak' or 'strong,' but by assessing their utility within the broader context of hadith verification.
en.seo_question: What is the biographical status of al-Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad al-Baṣrī in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.يُنْكَرُ: denied or rejected (in the context of hadith reliability)
key_terms.شَاهِدًا: a witness (used in hadith sciences to denote a narrator whose evidence is secondary or supportive)
